# Independent documentary TCP limit reference

Three new network-none containers restored the existing complete public stock snapshots. The previously reviewed UFW renderer produced a seven-field inbound TCP limit block, and its three raw lines were passed directly to real iptables/ip6tables binaries. The new mapping module was never imported by the collector. Both cases restore/verify the complete original policy before and after use; new containers were removed.

Cases cover host prefixes with port22 and finite network prefixes with port2222, for both address families under each exact22.04/24.04/26.04 tool triple. All addresses are documentary synthetic values. These records establish stock UFW combined compatibility/native mapping, not Docker provenance, target enrollment or authorization to mutate production.

`manifest.json` pins each original complete capture and the executed collector SHA. `collect_reference.py` preserves that collector with only the source directory resolved relative to this repository. It defaults to a plan-only report. Execution requires separately reviewed Docker permission and creates only new pinned-image network-none containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW, no host mounts/socket, and no image pulls. It never targets the existing lab VM.

The22.04 native TCP/conntrack/recent slots are opaque nulls.24/26 expose TCP dport and named conntrack/recent slots, but hide recent parameters. Complete exact selected arguments and whole raw agreement therefore remain mandatory. Native record counts or opaque slots alone never establish rule semantics.

Tests validate all six complete raw/selected/native states, reject changed fixed recent/conntrack parameters, and reject missing/duplicate/reordered rows. Existing stock grammar assets remain byte-identical; the extension accepts only the narrow finite-source single-TCP-port limit shape.
